A picture of the naval rivalry between the Royal Navy and the Kaiserilchemarine that led to a split between these royal cousins in Robert Massie's Dreadnaught.

If you like Tuchman, she also wrote a series of articles that were combined into a book titled The Proud Tower that sets up some of the political and anarchic uprisings that were occurring around the world in the 20 years prior to the outbreak of hostilities.

Martin Gilbert wrote a relatively short The First World War that provides battles, places and offensives across all the fronts, giving a somewhat clear overview of all the action that occurred. nice resource without putting too much analysis into it.

If you liked Massie, then pick up his Castles of Steel which detail the naval battles of the entire war, Pacific, Atlantic, North sea, etc.

Paris 1919 by Margaret MacMillan details the conference and its undertone, intrigues, and aftermath.
